newsitem.title: USA: Johnny Cash Headlines Kennedy Center Awards.
newsitem.headline: Johnny Cash Headlines Kennedy Center Awards.

text.p: - Country music star Johnny Cash got a lift to his legendary standing Sunday night with praise from the White House and acclaim from one of America's preeminent institutions for the arts.
"The Man in Black," whose fame is worldwide and whose life is seen by many as truly American, led the list of 1996 recipients for the annual Kennedy Centre Honours.
The other winners this year were: actor Jack Lemmon; ballerina Maria Tallchief; saxophonist Benny Carter, and playwright Edward Albee.

"He's a hard-edged rider dressed in black" who "redefined country music," President Bill Clinton said of Cash at a White House reception packed with entertainment luminaries, including country music stars Lyle Lovett and Emmylou Harris. They later performed at the awards show at the John F. Kennedy Centre for the Performing Arts.
"You've got our applause and admiration, and we've got your records," the president joked to Cash, who like him rose from rural roots in Arkansas to the world stage.
Among others paying tribute to Cash was Kris Kristofferson, who said Cash helped ignite his own singing career almost 30 years ago.
"It is such a gratifying thing to see his talent get the recognition it deserves," said Kristofferson of the Kennedy Centre Honours. "This goes way beyond country music."
Cash made his mark with a distinctive bass voice and a creative theme that transformed the stories of coal miners, sharecroppers, assembly line workers, trainmen, lovers and convicts into hit songs.
Some of his biggest chart-toppers were: "I Walk the Line," "Boy Named Sue," and the live album, "Johnny Cash at Folsom Prison."
